newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Burke ruled out for France test.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Burke ruled out for France test.

text.p: Fullback Matthew Burke was on Friday ruled out of Australia's starting line-up for next week's first rugby union test against France because of a groin injury.
But Australia coach Greg Smith was still hopeful Burke would be fit enough to take a place on the reserves bench against the Five Nations champions in Sydney on June 21.
Burke, whose absence is a major blow for the Wallabies ahead of the two-test series, will be replaced by Australian Capital Territory Brumbies fullback Stephen Larkham.
Smith said the early decision to leave Burke out of the starting line-up was taken to minimise disruption to the team's preparations in the week before the game.
"It's undecided yet whether Matt will be able to play on the bench or if he will stay with the team," Wallaby team manager John McKay told reporters after Burke failed a fitness test in training.
"Wallaby team doctor John Best advised Greg Smith that Matt would be unable to train for a few days and in the player's best interests, Matthew should be rested," he said.
No decision has yet been made as to a replacement if Burke is ruled out of the match altogether, McKay said.
Wallaby captain and lock John Eales is expected to take over goal kicking duties against France.
Burke aggravated the injury while playing for New South Wales in the domestic State of the Union match against Queensland in Brisbane last weekend.
Australia will host France in the second and final test in Brisbane on June 28.
